application_review: PROGRESS. The localized-dual-span round was rechecked before edits. Retained proof source hashes and axiom sets remain unchanged.

The generic algebra theorem explicitly assumes membership of the actual constant-one family and closure under each actual unit represented multiplier. These premises are not assumptions standing in for the desired localization: both are discharged by the previously audited localized-space theorems in the application.

For an actual represented member with pointwise bound B, normalization by B+1 yields an actual unit multiplier in the same space. Powers are constructed with pointwise bound B^n. Their membership follows inductively from unit multiplication and scalar closure. Polynomial representatives are actual finite linear combinations of these powers.

Continuous compositions are approximated on the fixed compact interval [-B,B] by real polynomials. The verified weighted Haar uniform distance bound and closedness give membership of the actual composition. No uniform B across all approximations is claimed.

The generic generated-span approximation supplies a uniformly bounded actual representative near the genuine projection. Its unit-interval clip remains in the same space, and the previously proved projection-clipping distance inequality preserves the approximation error. This gives actual unit-interval projection approximants.

The exact projection representative uses the already verified bounded diagonal theorem with reciprocal errors. The tail-containing-ultrafilter hypothesis is explicit. Pointwise interval bounds survive selection, and no countable intersection of large sets is assumed.

For a unit-interval actual function already in the original intersection, subtracting the actual localized projection leaves a unit residual. Since the localized span is contained in the intersection, this residual remains in both factors. It is orthogonal to the localized span by the genuine projection property, so the audited localized separation theorem makes it orthogonal to the first factor. Membership in that factor forces its Hilbert norm to zero.

To extend beyond represented unit inputs, first-factor hull generators are shifted and rescaled to [0,1]. Their second-factor projection has an exact unit-interval representative and remains in the first factor by the previously proved projection-preservation theorem. The unit-intersection argument places it in the localized span. Projection continuity and closedness extend the inclusion from the generator span to the entire first factor.

Every completed Hilbert vector in the original intersection is fixed by the second projection. This proves the reverse inclusion and the exact localized-span/intersection equality. The explicit approximation corollary returns an actual member of the original localized-family algebraic span with a pointwise uniform bound and arbitrarily small Hilbert error.

The primary Tao-Ziegler reference was reread at Corollary 6.4 and Section 7. The proved equality localizes the first dual construction to the second factor. Section 7 also localizes inside the intersection itself, with inputs retaining both factors, before its two-level recursion. That stronger input integration and the higher-order concatenation conclusion are not asserted by the current equality.

Ten theorems are audited. The localized generator-density equality is now proved under the displayed positive degrees, normalized nonnegative cell weights and tail-containing-ultrafilter hypothesis. Full higher-order concatenation, qualitative Bessel and the original StrongConjecture remain unproved.
remaining: The common-system master estimates, first-order Bessel, dual energy reduction, recursion and stability are proved. Exact arbitrary-vertex reflection of the actual subgroup cube law and mixed products is now proved. Mixed cubes now have exact arbitrary-vertex duality and weighted single-vertex replacement estimates. Finite products of dual functions now have quantitative empirical approximation uniform over bounded tests. Exact translated-product expansions and extraction for each fixed test are now proved. The exact mixed face split, projected-face correlation and one-step face Cauchy-Schwarz inequality are now proved. Face energies are now identified with actual copied cube means, with nonnegativity and copy algebra verified. Arbitrary-coordinate permutation invariance, copied-mean nonnegativity and reflection bounds are now established. Full multidimensional mixed Gowers Cauchy-Schwarz, the product-root bound and the single-vertex bound are now proved. Actual dual anti-uniformity, its weighted version and the finite zero-root orthogonality characterization are now proved. Mixed dual recursion, covariance and exact subgroup-shift expansions are now established. Same-subgroup mixed-dual finite products now have an exact averaged dual representation and retain weighted anti-uniformity. The actual unit-input mixed-dual convex hull now has multiplicative and translation closure with unchanged weighted anti-uniform bounds. For varying finite groups and cell types, the exact weighted Haar Hilbert realization and vanishing-Gowers/closed-dual-span orthogonality equivalence are now proved. The dual Hilbert span now has uniformly bounded scaled-hull representatives dense in its closure; their bound may depend on the approximation. Fixed-polynomial and continuous functional calculus for scaled-hull representatives, their clipping closure, and unit-interval-valued approximation of the actual dual Hilbert projection are now proved. The actual dual projection now controls the limiting Gowers power and yields unit-interval models with arbitrarily small Gowers error along the same ultrafilter. For ultrafilters containing every tail, diagonalization now provides one exact unit-interval representative of the dual projection and residual Gowers convergence to zero. Actual unit mixed-dual-hull multiplication now preserves the closed dual space and its orthogonal complement and satisfies the genuine projection pull-out identity on represented inputs. Every unit-bounded actual representative in the closed mixed-dual subspace now multiplies that subspace and its orthogonal complement into themselves. The genuine projection pull-out identity extends to these structured multipliers without requiring cellwise convex-hull membership. Actual translations, with shifts allowed to vary by stage and cell, act linearly on weighted-Haar L2-bounded families, preserve their Hilbert distances, and have inverse-shift adjoints. They preserve the closed mixed-dual subspace and its orthogonal complement; the genuine dual projection commutes with translation on actual represented inputs. Closed Hilbert subspaces containing every selected actual unit family now contain their internal finite averages, using fixed sample counts and the original weighted L2 variance bound. Finite products of unit represented structured inputs remain structured. Taking a mixed dual along any second subgroup system preserves the first closed dual space for such inputs. A unit represented member of the first space orthogonal to the intersection has vanishing second-system Gowers seminorm and is orthogonal to the entire second dual space. For tail-containing ultrafilters and positive degrees, actual dual projections now preserve the other closed dual space and commute on the entire completed Hilbert space. The proof first transfers orthogonality using actual unit-bounded projection representatives, proves unit-interval compatibility and an exact intersection model, then extends closed-space preservation from bounded generators by projection continuity and derives full commutation by self-adjointness. The first-order mixed dual is now identified with actual subgroup Haar averaging. Its unit hull consists of subgroup-invariant functions, and unit invariant functions belong to it. Actual first-order projections have exact unit Haar representatives. The first-order closed dual space is antitone in the subgroup, and its base concatenation is proved as the full equality of the two first-order spaces intersection with the first-order space of the subgroup sum, for every ultrafilter. The actual lower-order recursive coefficient now has a unit-bounded representative in both the lower first-direction dual space and the positive-degree second-direction dual space, for shifts varying by stage and cell. A dependent-selection argument gives uniform small correlation from vanishing correlation for every selected parameter family, without bounded cardinality assumptions. Orthogonality to the lower intersection therefore controls all these recursive coefficients uniformly along the ultrafilter. A tail-containing ultrafilter now supplies a positive uniform testing threshold from null testing of every dependent selected sequence, proved by slow-stage diagonalization. Every selected actual unit family in a positive-degree dual space therefore admits one eventual Gowers threshold controlling all parameters and all unit tests. The result also applies to fixed finite products of structured families and to recursive coefficients under the explicitly displayed lower-space containment. The original cube average is invariant under ambient translation. Averaging a pair-shift multiplicative derivative gives exactly the next cube order, and the corresponding Gowers moment identity preserves the original cell weights. A finite Haar testing estimate bounds mean absolute correlation by epsilon plus the next-order weighted Gowers power divided by a positive threshold power. Under an explicit eventual uniform small-test hypothesis, vanishing next-order Gowers values imply vanishing mean absolute correlation for varying finite subgroup systems along any filter. The actual mixed-dual families with unit inputs represented in the other dual space now generate a defined closed Hilbert subspace. Root normalization is proved harmless. This localized span contains the constant one and is contained in the original factor intersection when the other degree is positive. Finite products of localized actual duals lie in the localized closed span by an exact averaged dual representation and the verified internal-average theorem. Generic unit-generated spans have uniformly bounded actual algebraic-span representatives and dense actual approximants. Unit multipliers whose products with the generators lie in the closed span preserve that span, and pairwise generator closure extends to every actual unit represented member. Consequently actual unit members of the localized span multiply it into itself. An actual unit represented member of the other factor orthogonal to this localized span has vanishing first-factor Gowers value and is orthogonal to the entire first factor. A closed unit multiplier algebra containing the constant one now has actual power and polynomial representatives for uniformly bounded represented members, continuous functional calculus for such representatives, unit-interval approximants of its actual orthogonal projection, and an exact unit-interval projection representative for tail-containing ultrafilters. These results are discharged for the previously constructed localized dual span. Unit-interval actual members of the original factor intersection belong to that localized span: their residual after the localized projection remains in both original factors, and the localized separation theorem makes that residual orthogonal to the first factor, so it vanishes. Projection continuity extends this argument from bounded first-factor generators to the entire completed Hilbert space. Consequently the actual localized dual span is proved equal to the original factor intersection, with actual uniformly bounded algebraic-span approximants and unchanged cell weights. Localization inside the intersection itself, supplying actual inputs retaining both original factors for the two-level concatenation recursion, still needs to be integrated. Higher-order concatenation controlling dual correlations and the full qualitative Bessel theorem remain missing, as do remaining replica integration, cyclic-to-interval transfer and inverse correlator existence. Coloring-derived targets, Calibration/Alignment and final ordered positive rapidly separated monochromatic extraction remain. StrongConjecture is unchanged and unproved. No unavoidable blocker is established; publication, PR and prize application remain pending.
